title: Resume interrupted response streams without duplicating delivered output
before: At parent 3d1eba935f6a75d9e67adf667002700c5c592ec2, retryable socket-level stream failures could only restart the original request, and that replay was blocked after a content chunk had been yielded. Consequently, a long response cut after visible answer text propagated the transport error even when retries were configured. Thinking chunks also closed the older any-chunk replay gate despite carrying no visible answer that could be duplicated.
after: At d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5, retryable cuts with no accumulated visible text may replay the original request, while cuts after nonblank visible text enter a separately budgeted continuation path. The continuation request temporarily includes the delivered model text and a resume instruction, emits a continuation retry event so callers retain displayed text, accumulates repeated cuts with attempt-boundary overlap removal, and merges the delivered prefix into durable history after success. Function-call cuts are excluded, continuation state is discarded whenever a fresh restart supersedes it, and recovery stops after three continuation attempts.
diff: The change modifies packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts and geminiChat.test.ts. It adds a three-attempt continuation budget and shared resume-message construction; tracks visible text, function calls, per-attempt text, accumulated text, and staged prefixes; separates legal replay from continuation using accumulated visible output; builds synthetic continuation turns only in request contents; emits RETRY with isContinuation for resumptions; removes replayed overlap at attempt boundaries; resets staged continuation state on fresh-restart and reactive-compression paths; prepends the delivered prefix to the final model history turn with overlap deduplication and thought-part-aware placement; and adds regression tests for success, repeated cuts, overlap, history integrity, exclusions, supersession, and budget exhaustion.

    request, and that path is gated on `!streamYieldedChunk` — by the time a
    long answer is cut, chunks have obviously been delivered, so the gate was
    shut exactly when recovery was needed.
    
    Two changes:
    
    - Widen the replay gate from "any chunk yielded" to "visible output
      yielded" (non-blank answer text or a functionCall). Thinking models emit
      reasoning within seconds, which made replay unreachable for the very
      generations that need it. The UI's non-continuation RETRY handler clears
      the thought buffer, and the rate-limit and invalid-stream branches
      already re-send after thoughts have streamed, so this matches existing
      behaviour rather than adding risk.
    
    - Add continuation recovery for cuts that already delivered answer text,
      where replaying would duplicate what the caller has on screen. Keep the
      delivered text, ask the model to resume from it, and emit
      `{ RETRY, isContinuation: true }` so the UI keeps its text buffer — the
      same shape the MAX_TOKENS truncation path already uses. The synthetic
      turns are built into the request only, never written to `history`, so
      they cannot leak into the transcript or a later compression; on success
      the delivered prefix is merged back into the trailing model turn, with
      replayed overlap deduped by the existing recovery helper. Budget of 3,
      since one generation can be cut repeatedly by the same timeout.
    
    Cuts that delivered a `functionCall` are excluded: injecting a user turn
    between a `functionCall` and its `functionResponse` yields a sequence
    providers reject, and the scheduler's repair path already covers it.

    Review found that the `suppressNextRetryEvent` arm bypasses the
    continuation reset. Two branches emit a non-continuation RETRY *and* set
    `suppressNextRetryEvent`, so the next loop iteration takes the suppress
    arm and skips the `else if` that clears the staged continuation:
    
    - the transport replay branch, reachable when a continuation attempt is
      itself cut before yielding visible output, and
    - the reactive compression branch, which is if anything more likely on a
      continuation attempt, since that request carries the delivered text and
      the resume instruction on top of the original contents.

    request still asks the model to resume from it, and the merge on success
    writes that discarded text back into history — a permanent UI/history
    mismatch visible on `/compress` and `--resume`.
    
    Extract the reset into `resetTransportContinuation()` and call it from
    both branches before they set the flag. Resetting inside the suppress arm
    instead would clear the state of a continuation that is legitimately in
    flight.
    
    The pre-existing supersession test used `InvalidStreamError`, whose retry
    branch does not set `suppressNextRetryEvent`, so it exercised the
    `else if` path and neither trigger. Add a test per branch; both fail if
    their reset is removed.
    
    * fix(core): dedup replayed overlap when an intermediate cut is continued
    
    The continuation buffer accumulated each attempt's delivered text with a
    raw `+=`. Overlap dedup ran only at merge time, comparing the *final*
    attempt against the buffer, so an overlap replayed by an intermediate
    attempt was never stripped: it was baked into the buffer, sent in every
    later request, and merged into durable history.
    
    Reachable because maxContinuationRetries is 3, so two cuts fit in one
    send. Attempt 1 delivers "part one " and is cut; attempt 2 replays its
    tail as "part one part two " and is cut too. The buffer became
    "part one part one part two " — corrupting /compress, --resume, and the
    context of every later turn.

    running attempt's text, and the catch path folds it into the accumulated
    buffer through getRecoveryContinuationSuffix, stripping whatever that
    attempt replayed. Deduping per chunk instead would be wrong: the overlap
    scan is suffix-anchored, so it would eat legitimately repeated text
    mid-stream. The attempt boundary is the only place a replay can occur.
    
    Also covers the two untested branches of the delivered-text merge, both
    of which already behaved correctly: a continuation leading with a thought
    part (the text merges into the text part, not ahead of the thinking) and
    one that finishes with only a thought part (the delivered text is
    inserted after it). Without coverage a regression in the insert position
    would silently misplace text in history.
    
    276 tests pass in geminiChat.test.ts; tsc and eslint clean.
    
    * fix(core): keep continuing when a later attempt is cut before it delivers
    
    The replay gate tests `!streamYieldedContentChunk`, which is declared inside
    the attempt loop and therefore per-attempt. That cannot distinguish "nothing
    has been delivered to the caller" from "this attempt was cut before delivering
    anything, after earlier attempts already put text on screen" — and only the
    first is replayable. Because the replay branch is checked before the
    continuation branch, the second case fell into it: `resetTransportContinuation()`
    dropped the accumulated text and a plain RETRY (no `isContinuation`) told the UI
    to discard output the user was watching, after which the model regenerated it
    from scratch.
    
    Reachable two ways once a continuation is in flight, both with
    `transportStreamRetryCount` still 0 so the replay budget is intact:
    
      - attempt 1 delivers "part one " -> continuation; attempt 2 is cut while
        still in its thinking phase, so it yields only a thought part and
        `streamYieldedContentChunk` is false;
      - the same, with attempt 2 cut having yielded nothing at all.
    
    Gate the replay branch on the accumulated buffer being empty as well. The two
    gates are now exact complements (`=== 0` here, `> 0` on the continuation
    branch), so a retryable transport cut after any delivered text always
    continues and never replays. The `resetTransportContinuation()` call inside the
    branch now has nothing to clear; it stays as an assertion of that invariant so
    a future gate change cannot leak staged text into a restarted attempt.
    
    `drops a pending continuation when a replay takes over` asserted the old
    behaviour for the yielded-nothing case — it was written to pin the design's
    internal consistency, not a user-visible requirement, and that premise is what
    this fixes. Rewritten as `keeps continuing when a later attempt is cut with
    nothing yielded`, asserting the delivered text survives into the third request
    and into history. The sibling tests covering the *other* plain-RETRY paths
    (fresh-restart retry, reactive compression) are unchanged and still pass:
    those genuinely do discard the delivered text, and reaching them still resets.
    
    Also extracts the resume instruction shared verbatim by
    OUTPUT_RECOVERY_MESSAGE and TRANSPORT_CONTINUATION_MESSAGE into
    RECOVERY_RESUME_INSTRUCTION. Only the lead-in sentence naming the cause
    differed, so tuning the wording on one path silently left the other on the old
    text. Both resulting strings are byte-identical to before.
    
    277 tests pass in geminiChat.test.ts; both new tests verified failing without
    the source change. tsc --noEmit and eslint clean.

    The comment claimed the fold runs on both exits from an attempt. It runs
    only in the catch block; the success exit merges the continuation prefix
    into history and breaks without folding.
    
    No behaviour change — every read of the accumulated buffer is inside the
    catch, after the fold. But the comment would mislead anyone adding a
    post-loop read, which would silently omit the last attempt's text, so the
    note now says which exit folds and what a new reader would have to do.

episode.title: Resume interrupted response streams without duplicating delivered output
episode.before: At parent 3d1eba935f6a75d9e67adf667002700c5c592ec2, retryable socket-level stream failures could only restart the original request, and that replay was blocked after a content chunk had been yielded. Consequently, a long response cut after visible answer text propagated the transport error even when retries were configured. Thinking chunks also closed the older any-chunk replay gate despite carrying no visible answer that could be duplicated.
episode.after: At d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5, retryable cuts with no accumulated visible text may replay the original request, while cuts after nonblank visible text enter a separately budgeted continuation path. The continuation request temporarily includes the delivered model text and a resume instruction, emits a continuation retry event so callers retain displayed text, accumulates repeated cuts with attempt-boundary overlap removal, and merges the delivered prefix into durable history after success. Function-call cuts are excluded, continuation state is discarded whenever a fresh restart supersedes it, and recovery stops after three continuation attempts.
episode.diff: The change modifies packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts and geminiChat.test.ts. It adds a three-attempt continuation budget and shared resume-message construction; tracks visible text, function calls, per-attempt text, accumulated text, and staged prefixes; separates legal replay from continuation using accumulated visible output; builds synthetic continuation turns only in request contents; emits RETRY with isContinuation for resumptions; removes replayed overlap at attempt boundaries; resets staged continuation state on fresh-restart and reactive-compression paths; prepends the delivered prefix to the final model history turn with overlap deduplication and thought-part-aware placement; and adds regression tests for success, repeated cuts, overlap, history integrity, exclusions, supersession, and budget exhaustion.

when_to_use: A response stream can terminate because of a retryable socket or transport failure after streaming has begun.
The stream owner can distinguish visible answer text from internal reasoning or blank output.

Do not retain continuation state after a fresh restart has instructed the caller to discard prior output.

No mechanism exists to preserve the caller's output buffer across a retry event.
The streamed protocol cannot safely represent prior output plus a resume instruction in a subsequent request.
The interrupted output contains a structured call that requires an immediate paired response.

title: Honor server retry advice without restarting its countdown
before: At parent ab021e9f137c9daacf6ae06a495f3c7d6199fab2, HTTP retry loops ignored Retry-After and always used local exponential backoff. Retry delays carried by higher-level errors were relative durations, so time spent reading bodies, mapping errors, emitting notifications, or otherwise propagating an error could restart or extend the server-requested wait. Expired server advice was therefore indistinguishable from missing advice and could incorrectly fall back to local backoff.
after: At 9d8de196748b57d7f463a7757eaa447b6483a331, retry advice is parsed when received into a monotonic absolute deadline supporting delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms. commit.subject: Honor Retry-After and preserve server retry deadlines (#47641)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

HTTP retries used local backoff even when the server supplied `Retry-After`. Relative retry delays also failed to account for time spent propagating errors or reporting retries.

## What changed

- Parse `Retry-After` delay seconds and HTTP dates into a monotonic deadline captured when response headers arrive.
- Honor that deadline for HTTP retries, falling back to local backoff when valid advice is absent.
- Preserve deadlines through API and Bedrock error mapping, stream retries, and exhausted retry state. Expired advice remains a zero delay instead of triggering local backoff.

## Testing

Add coverage for header parsing, deadline countdown and expiry, error mapping after exhausted HTTP retries, and delayed stream retry notifications. Update Responses and remote compaction tests

episode.before: At parent ab021e9f137c9daacf6ae06a495f3c7d6199fab2, HTTP retry loops ignored Retry-After and always used local exponential backoff. Retry delays carried by higher-level errors were relative durations, so time spent reading bodies, mapping errors, emitting notifications, or otherwise propagating an error could restart or extend the server-requested wait. Expired server advice was therefore indistinguishable from missing advice and could incorrectly fall back to local backoff.
episode.after: At 9d8de196748b57d7f463a7757eaa447b6483a331, retry advice is parsed when received into a monotonic absolute deadline supporting delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms. That deadline is attached to transport and semantic errors, retained through API and provider mappings and exhausted retry state, and used by HTTP and stream retry loops with sleep-until semantics. Invalid or absent advice still uses local backoff; explicit zero or expired valid advice remains present as a zero remaining delay.
episode.diff: The change adds the RetryAfter deadline value and parser; captures it from unsuccessful HTTP response headers before body processing; replaces relative retry-delay fields across transport, API, provider, protocol, and streaming layers; makes request and stream retries wait for the original deadline while retaining local backoff as the no-advice fallback; and adds unit, mapping, virtual-time, and end-to-end tests for parsing, countdown, expiry, delayed notification, exhausted retries, and successful recovery. The commit changes 28 files with 429 insertions and 86 deletions.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 9d8de196748b57d7f463a7757eaa447b6483a331 with parent ab021e9f137c9daacf6ae06a495f3c7d6199fab2; its commit message states that HTTP retries used local backoff despite Retry-After and relative delays failed to account for propagation and reporting time.
The commit modifies 28 files with 429 insertions and 86 deletions, spanning HTTP transport, request retries, API/error mappings, stream retry state, provider adaptation, and tests.

RetryAfter stores a monotonic Instant, parses nonnegative delta-seconds or an HTTP date, exposes the original deadline, and computes a saturating remaining delay so expired advice remains zero rather than becoming absent.
Both buffered and streaming HTTP transport paths parse Retry-After from response headers as soon as an unsuccessful response arrives and attach the captured deadline to TransportError::Http.
The HTTP retry loop prefers the attached server deadline, records its current remaining delay, sleeps until the absolute deadline, and uses jittered local backoff only when advice is absent.

API error mapping extracts RetryAfter before changing the semantic error variant and reattaches the same value afterward, preserving advice across retryable, rate-limit, overload, and HTTP transport mappings.

CodexErr now retains RetryAfter, derives remaining server delay from its original deadline, distinguishes expired valid advice from missing advice, and continues to apply retryability and retry-budget policy independently of the presence of advice.

The stream retry handler retains the original server deadline across asynchronous user notification, sleeps until that deadline, and stores it when stream retries are exhausted; the special unbounded connection-retry and transport-fallback branches retain their separate policies.

Parser tests prove delta-seconds count down to zero, HTTP dates map to the monotonic clock, explicit zero and past dates remain valid zero-delay advice, and malformed or overflowing values are rejected.
A virtual-time stream test delays retry notification and proves the retry still resumes at the originally captured deadline rather than waiting a fresh relative duration.
An integration test serves a 503 with Retry-After: 1, observes HTTP-layer retry telemetry, verifies at least one second elapses before retry, and confirms recovery with exactly two response requests.

A virtual-time integration test proves the final HTTP retry error retains its later server deadline through API mapping, reports the decreasing remaining delay, and still reports Some(Duration::ZERO) after expiry.
Provider-specific error rewriting is tested to preserve the original retry deadline rather than replacing it while changing the user-facing error details.
The parent implementation contained an explicit TODO in the HTTP retry loop and always selected local backoff before sleeping for a relative delay.

candidate_workflows.name: honor-server-retry-deadlines-across-layered-recovery
candidate_workflows.title: Honor server retry deadlines across layered recovery
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution workflow for systems where retry advice crosses transport, semantic-error, provider, and streaming boundaries before the next attempt is scheduled.

workflow_graph.goal: Make every eligible retry honor the server's originally requested earliest retry time without restarting the countdown during error propagation and without replacing established retry policy when advice is unavailable.
when_to_use: A client receives retry timing from HTTP headers or streamed errors but currently retries using only local backoff.
Retry advice passes through multiple error mappings, notifications, provider adapters, or exhausted-retry state before reuse.
Observed retry waits begin too late because each layer stores or reconstructs a relative duration.
anti_goals: Do not make terminal failures retryable merely because they carry retry advice.
Do not expand configured retry budgets or remove existing transport-fallback and unbounded connection-retry policies.
Do not replace local backoff for failures with missing or invalid server advice.
Do not treat an expired valid deadline as missing advice and introduce a new backoff delay.
not_applicable_when: The upstream protocol supplies no retry timing and local backoff is already the intended complete policy.
The operation is not safely retryable or retry eligibility cannot be established independently of timing advice.
Retry timing never crosses an asynchronous or abstraction boundary and an existing absolute-deadline representation is already preserved end to end.
inputs: Raw server retry-advice headers or streamed delay signal
Clock facilities supporting a monotonic deadline
Transport and semantic error types crossed by the failure
Retry eligibility rules and configured retry budgets
Local fallback-backoff policy
Request and stream retry call sites
Deterministic clock-controlled and end-to-end recovery tests
workflow_graph.entry_state: Retryable failures may contain server advice, but request retries ignore it or higher layers carry relative durations that can restart during propagation.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Valid advice is captured once, preserved unchanged across all relevant error boundaries, and consumed as an absolute deadline by eligible retry schedulers; invalid or absent advice uses local backoff, while zero or expired valid advice produces an immediate eligible retry rather than fallback delay.

steps.condition: Required when the failure source can provide server retry timing.
steps.validation: Parser and transport tests establish accepted formats, receipt-time capture, countdown, expiry, and invalid-value behavior.

steps.condition: Required for every error translation, reclassification, provider rewrite, or exhausted-retry record between receipt and scheduling.
steps.validation: Mapping tests assert the same deadline survives translation and its remaining delay continues to decrease through elapsed virtual time.

steps.condition: Required only after existing policy independently declares the failure retryable and budget remains; use local backoff when no valid deadline exists.
steps.validation: Virtual-time and end-to-end tests prove sleep-until behavior, delayed-notification accounting, local-backoff fallback, bounded attempts, telemetry, and successful recovery.

validation_ladder: Unit-test parsing of delta-seconds, HTTP dates, explicit zero, expired dates, malformed values, and overflow.
Test transport capture before body processing and verify advice is attached to unsuccessful-response errors.
Test each error-mapping boundary for deadline identity and decreasing remaining duration.
Use paused time to prove intervening notification or propagation work consumes the original wait rather than preceding a fresh delay.
Verify no-advice failures still use bounded jittered backoff and retry eligibility remains independent of advice.
Run end-to-end recovery with a mock server, retry telemetry, elapsed-time assertion, successful completion, and exact request count.
Exercise retry exhaustion and confirm the last captured deadline remains available and becomes zero rather than absent after expiry.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the response-arrival boundary cannot be identified reliably enough to capture advice once.
Stop if retryability or idempotency is unresolved; timing advice alone must not authorize another attempt.
Stop if an error-mapping boundary drops metadata and cannot be changed or tested without altering a public compatibility contract.
Stop when retry budget is exhausted or the existing policy classifies the error as terminal, while retaining advice only if downstream recovery state explicitly requires it.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation leaves a TODO for honoring server advice before switching from WebSockets to fallback HTTP transport.
The buffered execute path notes that retry advice is not preserved when unbounded diagnostic-body reading itself fails with a network or timeout classification.
Wrapped WebSocket HTTP errors introduced in this change still populate retry_after as None rather than parsing their available headers.
